seoTitle: How to Set Email Forwarding & Routing in Workspace Gmail
metaDescription: Learn how to configure email forwarding and routing rules in Gmail through the Google Workspace Admin Console for secure, reliable delivery.
intro: Forwarding and routing rules let admins automatically redirect incoming mail, manage shared inboxes, or handle employee transitions without losing messages. This guide covers how to set these up correctly through the Google Workspace Admin Console.

steps.heading: Open the Admin Console's Gmail settings
steps.body: Sign in as an admin and navigate to the Gmail section under Apps to access routing and forwarding controls.

steps.heading: Create a routing rule
steps.body: Set up a rule that defines how incoming or outgoing mail should be handled, such as forwarding all mail from one address to another.

steps.heading: Configure forwarding for specific users or groups
steps.body: Apply the rule to individual users, groups, or the whole organization depending on your needs, like handling an employee exit or shared inbox.

steps.heading: Follow best practices to avoid errors
steps.body: Test routing rules carefully before applying them broadly, since misconfigured rules can cause emails to loop or fail to deliver.

steps.heading: Monitor and adjust as needed
steps.body: Check delivery logs periodically to confirm forwarding is working as expected and adjust rules if business needs change.

faq.question: Can I set up forwarding for just one user instead of the whole organization?
faq.answer: Yes, routing rules in the Admin Console can be scoped to specific users or groups rather than applying organization-wide.

faq.question: What's the difference between forwarding and routing in Gmail?
faq.answer: Forwarding sends a copy of incoming mail to another address, while routing rules can apply more complex logic like rejecting, rerouting, or duplicating messages based on conditions.

faq.question: Will forwarding rules affect email security?
faq.answer: If set up carelessly, forwarding rules can expose sensitive information, so it's important to only route mail to trusted, verified addresses.

faq.question: Can I use routing rules when an employee leaves the company?
faq.answer: Yes, this is a common use case — routing an outgoing employee's mail to a manager or shared inbox ensures nothing important is missed.
